pack.name: Pulse Admin Insights Starter Pack
pack.description: Prebuilt Tableau Pulse metric definitions on the standard Admin Insights data sources. Deploy-anywhere, basic specifications only. MVP scope: nine event-log trend metrics across three clusters.
pack.spec_notes: Manifest is the tool's intermediate representation. deploy.py resolves each source name to its site LUID at run time and maps these entries to Pulse CreateDefinitionRequest payloads. Filter values marked confirm:true must be verified against live data via query-datasource at build time. Aggregation enums COUNT, COUNT_DISTINCT, SUM, and AVERAGE are all confirmed: metrics using each have been created and rendered on a live site. MVP is deliberately limited to event/activity-log sources (TS Events, Viz Load Times, Job Performance), which retain real history and trend honestly in Pulse. Current-state snapshot sources (TS Users, Site Content, Subscriptions) full-refresh daily and retain no history, so they are held out of the MVP; see deferred sections. Adjustable dimensions are set PER METRIC, not per cluster: each list is drawn from fields that exist on the source, returns real values for that metric (a dimension pinned by the metric's own filter is omitted), and favors low/medium-cardinality categorical fields so Pulse top-contributor insights stay clean. High-cardinality identity fields (Actor User Name, Item LUID, raw Item Name on TS Events) are deliberately excluded as default breakdowns.

metrics.name: Active Users
metrics.description: Distinct people who took any action on the site during the period. The clearest single adoption signal; higher is better.
metrics.why: The single clearest adoption signal. Distinct people doing anything on the site over the period.

metrics.name: Site Logins
metrics.description: How often people sign in, counting login events. Shows whether Tableau is part of the daily routine; higher is better.
metrics.why: Login frequency shows whether Tableau is part of the daily routine or an occasional visit.

filters.verified: Confirmed against live TS Events: value is 'Login' (not 'Sign In').

metrics.dimensions_note: Intentionally thin. Sign-in events are not performed against content, so Project, Item Type, and Workbook are null. Role and license are the only breakdowns that carry meaning.

metrics.name: Content Views
metrics.description: How many times content was accessed over the period. The core measure of value delivered; higher is better. Note: this counts all access events, including automated renders from subscriptions and alerts, so it reflects total views served rather than human views only.
metrics.why: How much content is actually being consumed. The core value-delivered metric.

filters.verified: Item Type values confirmed: View / Workbook / Data Source.
Event Type = Access confirmed against live data.

metrics.name: Unique Content Accessed
metrics.description: Distinct pieces of content accessed during the period. Breadth of use, not just volume; higher is better.
metrics.why: Breadth of use. A high view count on a shrinking set of content is a different story than broad use.

filters.verified: Event Type = Access confirmed against live data.

metrics.name: Assets Published
metrics.description: Distinct pieces of content published during the period, counting each asset once no matter how many times it was republished. Includes both brand-new content and updates to existing content (the event log has no first-publish flag to separate them). Higher is better.
metrics.why: Creation and update activity. Shows whether the community is producing content, not just consuming it. Counting distinct assets avoids inflating the number when one item is republished many times.

filters.verified: Confirmed against live TS Events: content publishing is Event Type 'Publish' (Publish Data Source/View/Workbook). 'Create' is administrative object creation, not content.

metrics.name: Average View Load Time
metrics.description: Average time to load a view. The speed users actually feel; lower is better.
metrics.why: The experience users actually feel. Slow loads are the fastest way to lose adoption.

filters.verified: Confirmed against live Viz Load Times: the successful-render bucket is 'Success'. Excludes error and redirect responses so the average reflects loads that actually rendered.

metrics.dimensions_note: Status Code Type is pinned to 'Success' by this metric's filter, so it is omitted as a breakdown.

metrics.name: Load Errors
metrics.description: View requests that returned a client or server error instead of rendering. A reliability signal separate from speed; lower is better.
metrics.why: Failed requests that never render. A reliability signal separate from speed.
metrics.dimensions_note: Status Code Type is kept as a breakdown even though it is filtered, because the filter admits two values (Client errors, Server errors) and splitting them is diagnostic.

metrics.name: Extract Refresh Failures
metrics.description: Extract-refresh jobs that ended in failure during the period. Final Job Result records only Succeeded or Failed, so this counts every refresh that did not succeed. Each failure points at a specific schedule or item to fix; lower is better.
metrics.why: Failed refreshes mean stale dashboards. The most actionable admin health metric.

filters.verified: Confirmed against live Job Performance metadata: Final Job Result is a two-state calculated field (Succeeded or Failed only). 'Failed' therefore captures every refresh that did not succeed; there are no separate Timed Out or Cancelled values to include.

Admin Insights Job Performance uses raw job-type enums. Extract refreshes are 'RefreshExtracts' and 'RefreshExtractsViaBridge' (there is no 'Extract Refresh' value). Confirmed against live data 2026-09.

metrics.name: Average Job Duration
metrics.description: Average run time of jobs that completed successfully, in seconds. Failed jobs are excluded so aborted or hung runs don't distort the average. Rising durations are an early warning of capacity pressure; lower is better.
metrics.why: Rising job durations signal capacity pressure before it turns into failures. Measuring only successful runs keeps the average about healthy throughput, not failures.

filters.verified: Confirmed against live Job Performance metadata: Final Job Result is a two-state field (Succeeded or Failed). Filtering to Succeeded measures healthy-job runtime and excludes failures that abort early or hang.

deferred_cohort_and_snapshot.note: Held out of the MVP. Cohort metrics trend on a creation date and draw a real line, but sit on current-state snapshot sources, so older periods progressively undercount as users/content are deleted (survivorship bias). Snapshot metrics have no source history at all (daily full refresh overwrites prior state), so they cannot trend or compare period over period, and the license fields are FIXED site-level calcs that Pulse basic specs may reject. Candidates for a later version, likely alongside a purpose-built fact source that banks daily snapshots.

metrics.name: Data Source Connections
metrics.reason: Clean event, but a narrower governed-data signal; second-tier for the adoption story.

metrics.name: New Users
metrics.reason: Survivorship bias on a snapshot source.

metrics.name: Content Growth
metrics.reason: Survivorship bias on a snapshot source.

metrics.name: New Subscriptions & Metric Follows
metrics.reason: Weak cohort on a snapshot source.

metrics.name: Subscriptions Delivered
metrics.reason: Counts by Last Sent, a single most-recent-send timestamp per subscription, not a delivery log.

metrics.name: Occupied Licenses
metrics.reason: No source history; FIXED site-level calc.

metrics.name: Remaining Licenses
metrics.reason: No source history; FIXED site-level calc.

metrics.name: Site Storage Used (MB)
metrics.reason: No source history; SUM double-counts across item types.

deferred_advanced_tier.name: Inactive Users (>90 days)
deferred_advanced_tier.needs: measure threshold expression on Days Since Last Login

deferred_advanced_tier.name: Stale Content (>90 days)
deferred_advanced_tier.needs: DATEDIFF expression on Last Accessed At
